messages:
leah: Heads-up — Acme Labs reporting intermittent 502s and very high token latency since the canary model rollout ~14:42 UTC. They sent a couple of request ids: 20240315T144223-8a7f9c, 20240315T144301-3b2d1e, 20240315T144402-fc0a11. Sometimes response is 200 but body truncated. They are on hosted. Can someone help repro and advise rollback?

marco: Thanks. Can you paste the exact request-id header values the client got from the response (if any) and the full curl they used? We need model param, approximate prompt length, and whether they used streaming or normal. Also include account id.

leah: Copying what I have: account=acme-labs-prod-12, model param sent by client = "redwood-alpha-canary-v2", prompt length ~800 tokens, non-streaming POST. Response body from our API (one example): {"error":"upstream error","request_id":"20240315T144223-8a7f9c"}
They used this curl (sanitized):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-canary-v2","input":"<~800 tokens prompt>"}' \
  --max-time 60 -v
```

marco: OK — two immediate asks to reproduce in our env: 1) run with --include/ -i (so response headers with our request id are captured), and 2) set a distinct X-Request-ID header so we can correlate in logs. Ask the customer to run:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: acme-20240315-01" \
  --data-raw '{"model":"redwood-alpha-canary-v2","input":"<same prompt>"}' \
  --max-time 30
```

marco: Please send me the full response headers, body, and the exact X-Request-ID value the client used. I will tail runtime logs for that id.

anita: Heads-up from SRE — we've seen a similar pattern when a canary model variant had a kernel/quant mismatch for larger sequence lengths. The runtime tries GPU, falls back to CPU or a different kernel, memory alloc spikes, and some requests get 502s rather than graceful fallback. If the prompt is ~800 tokens it's in the red for this canary on some GPU types.

anita: Quick repro step for us (will do once we have request-id): grep the id in inference runtime logs:

```bash
sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime -o short-iso | rg 20240315T144223-8a7f9c -n
# look for kernel/memory/fallback lines
```

ryan: From ops — deploy-bot shows the canary rollout paused automatically at 14:50 UTC for inference-prod (snapshot id dpl-20240315-7). I can pause/rollback full rollout if eng requests.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for service=inference-prod at 2024-03-15T14:50:12Z (pause reason: error rate spike).

leah: I've asked the customer to run marco's curl and attach the support debug bundle (they have the support-bundle script). They've sent back the curl output with headers for id=acme-20240315-01 and the response: 502 + body referencing request_id 20240315T144301-3b2d1e. Sending now.

marco: Got the bundle. Log snippet shows: 

```
[2024-03-15T14:44:21Z] ERROR req=20240315T144223-8a7f9c runtime: attempt_gpu_load(model=redwood-alpha-canary-v2) -> kernel_mismatch; falling back to cpu_exec; alloc_fail -> returning upstream 502
[2024-03-15T14:44:22Z] WARN req=20240315T144301-3b2d1e runtime: fallback path increased latency 3.2s; client timeout observed
```

marco: Repro steps confirmed on our side with a local run using that prompt length + canary variant — the canary kernel selection fails on older CUDA drivers we have in one pool. There are two immediate mitigations: 1) pin this account to the stable model (redwood-alpha-stable-v7) while we fix kernel selection, or 2) update routing policy to prefer stable when prompt length > 512.

anita: If you want a quick rollback, ops can flip the rollout back to stable for inference-prod. That will stop new traffic to canary while we patch.

ryan: I can trigger a rollback now. Doing a controlled rollback to stable shard routing — ETA ~3m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

leah: Customer asked for ETA — told them 10m for mitigation and asked them to confirm after we flip.

marco: Postmortem actions (short):
- capture kernel compatibility matrix and add to model onboarding checklist
- add an automatic routing rule: if model variant reports kernel_mismatch events > threshold, reduce canary weight to 0 and alert
- add a better error surface: on fallback to CPU, return 200 with a notice or structured error that includes runtime fallback metadata so callers can retry or pin automatically

leah: RE customer — will ask them to confirm they see stable responses after rollback and collect any final request ids. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

anita: Note: if customer needs immediate manual pin, they can use the account-level override API (ask support for pin-token) or I can coordinate with platform to set it.

marco: I logged an internal ticket INF-1429 and attached the debug bundle + logs. Assigning to eng-runtime to follow up on kernel selection and better fallback semantics.

leah: Closing loop with customer now.
